approved.title: Reducing obesity in the UK
approved.question: What does recent academic and grey literature say about which policies, programmes and interventions can reduce obesity in the UK, for whom, and under what delivery conditions?
scoping_notes: Setting: UK.
Policy aim: reduce obesity.
screening_criteria: Include UK study or programme settings.
Include interventions, policies or programmes aiming to prevent or reduce obesity.
Include obesity, weight, diet, physical activity or purchasing outcomes.
Include empirical studies, evaluations, reviews, modelling studies and policy reports.
Exclude documents with no obesity-reduction intervention or policy focus.
Exclude opinion pieces with no evidence base.

component_rationale.characterise: Included to map the range of obesity-reduction approaches, populations, settings and evidence gaps across the corpus.
component_rationale.screen_full: Included because the broad framing is likely to retrieve documents that mention obesity but are not actually about reducing it in the UK.
component_rationale.select: Included to prioritise the strongest-fit and most policy-relevant documents for synthesis emphasis.
component_rationale.extract: Excluded at standard depth; deep extraction would be useful if you want intervention-by-intervention findings in more detail.
component_rationale.group: Excluded because grouping extracted findings only runs with the deep extraction chain.

approved.expected_artefact_shape: grounded answer over the screened corpus
assumptions: I have interpreted “Reduce obesity in the UK” as a request for evidence on interventions, policies and programmes that could reduce obesity in UK populations.
No population subgroup was specified, so I would keep adults, children and whole-population approaches in scope.
No intervention type was specified, so I would include fiscal, regulatory, environmental, service-delivery, community, school, workplace and clinical/public-health approaches.
No outcomes were specified, so I would include obesity-related weight outcomes and credible intermediate outcomes such as diet, physical activity and purchasing where linked to obesity prevention.
No date window was given; I suggest focusing on evidence published from 2015 onwards, with older landmark reviews likely picked up only where recent sources cite them.
I would not apply UK publisher or author-affiliation filters: those filter source origin, not study setting, and could miss non-UK authors writing about UK interventions.

turns.text: I’ve drafted this as a broad UK policy evidence review: what interventions, programmes and policies can reduce obesity in the UK, including who they work for and what delivery conditions matter. I propose a standard search and standard analysis: broad enough to cover academic and grey literature, with a full-text precision screen and purposive selection of the strongest-fit documents for synthesis emphasis. The UK constraint is expressed as a screening rule for study/programme setting rather than a backend geography filter, because publisher country and author affiliation filters only capture where the source comes from, not what country the intervention is about. If you want a lighter horizon scan or a deeper intervention-by-intervention extraction, we can adjust before running.
